newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch expand swine fever area as new cases appear.
newsitem.headline: Dutch expand swine fever area as new cases appear.

text.p: The Dutch farm ministry said on Friday that due to further cases of swine fever appearing, it had expanded the area in the south of country in which pigs are bought up by the authorities and destroyed.

There are now some 217 cases of swine fever in the Netherlands and the disease which came to light in February is showing no signs of abating. Earlier this week Farm Minister Jozias van Aartsen said the toll would probably rise to 300.
Within the same area, the transport of all livestock and manure is also banned, a measure in force for some months.

The ministry said more than two million pigs had now been destoyed in attempts to contain the outbreak, which has seriously impacted farmers' incomes, and it admitted there was still no sign of it subsiding.
"We had seven cases appear yesterday, so you can't really say there's a sign of it stopping," a ministry spokeswoman said.

Sha added the European Commission, which is providing around 70 percent of compensation to farmers affected, had agreed to the new measure. Van Aartsen said earlier this week, the total bill for the disease was running at one billion guilders.
Many of the Netherlands' key trading partners, including the United States, have halted imports of Dutch pigs and porkmeat.
Exports of such products earned the Netherlands more than five billion guilders in 1996.

The Dutch government is pinning its hopes on a new type of marker vaccine, which it say will allow the easier segregation of infected anaimals. It hopes to have the vaccine, developed by Dutch scientists, in use by the beginning of next year.
This latest outbreak is the first in the Netherlands since 1992. Before the culling, there were 14 million pigs in the country.
